newsitem.title: UK: Options - Market at ease in coffee, wary in cocoa.
newsitem.headline: Options - Market at ease in coffee, wary in cocoa.

text.p: Volatility sales in LIFFE coffee options pointed to expectations for a steady market in the near-term, but higher cocoa volatilities revealed investor doubts over cocoa's recent gains, traders said on Thursday.
Strangle and straddle sales in May coffee options kept May volatilities under pressure most of the week, traders said.
Those volatility sales were seen as an indication investors were comfortable with coffee futures near current levels and that May volatilities would continue to fall.
Despite one aggressive buyer of 400 May $1,750 calls to set a new position on Wednesday, May coffee volatility has fallen to about 38 to 40 percent, traders said.

Traders saw the May $1,750 call purchase as expensive between 44 and 45 percent volatility, but they said volatility did not spike up on the trade because it was spread out throughout the day on offers already in the market.

LIFFE robusta coffee futures were down in early trade on Thursday, but traders expected May to remain between $1,600 and $1,700 in the near-term. May has been rangebound since falling to about a one-month low last week.

But further out, the outlook for coffee was more muddled. July and September volatilities were holding firm, near 45 percent, creating a large skew between the May and July volatilities, traders said.
On Thursday morning, floor sources said some interest in coffee options had moved into the $1,800 strike in nearby months.
In cocoa options, traders said activity was fairly quiet with the most noteworthy activity seen in July 1,150 stg calls. Traders said a trade house bought 200 of those calls.
Despite the lack of activity in cocoa options, traders noted that volatility jumped to the highest level in about 18 months.
Volatility in July cocoa options was pegged near 38 percent, up from about 22 percent before this week's sharp rally, a sign the market was wary of cocoa's recent gains.
LIFFE May cocoa climbed to a 7-1/2 month high on Wednesday, following the CSCE's 2-1/2 year high, before losing 2 stg to 1,054 stg per tonne on light profit-taking at 1018 GMT on Thursday.
Gains were mostly seen as technical as chart formations turned bullish after a short-covering wave.
But some analysts and traders have been sceptical of the rally, saying that fundamentals did not justify sharply higher cocoa prices.

They said expectations for a large Ivorian crop, speculative selling before first notice day on April 17 in New York and forecasts for lower European grinds this week and next could cap gains. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8072
